name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district with a long-serving incumbent, Jared Huffman, seeking another term
Huffman holds a decisive money edge: about $978,000 raised and $1.1 million on hand versus no reported fundraising from Robin Littau
No outside spending against Huffman and no competitive warning signs in available data
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
model.rationale: Huffman combines a heavily Democratic North Coast seat, incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage against a challenger with no visible campaign resources, and markets price the race accordingly. With no polls or ratings flagging risk, the fundamentals point to a wide Democratic win.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Huffman or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though an outright upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
California's North Coast district leans heavily Democratic, and Jared Huffman has held the seat since 2013, giving him the full advantages of incumbency in a D+13 seat. He has raised about $978,000 and reports more than $1 million on hand, while Republican Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising or cash reserves in the available data. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and campaign finance.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent, in line with the structural advantages on the Democratic side. No outside money is opposing Huffman, and the challenger lacks the resources typically needed to compete in a seat this favorable to the incumbent. The expected margin sits in the low twenties, and the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
